issues.description: The problem statement requires implementing a function named `print_newline`, but the solution defines a label `print_nl` instead. The template also does not provide a `print_newline` stub. This name mismatch between specification and solution (and absence in the template) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the exact symbol they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the function name across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution label `print_nl` to `print_newline` (and keep or add a matching stub in the template), or (B) change the problem statement to require `print_nl`. Additionally add a small stub for `print_newline` in the template (e.g., `print_newline: \n    ret`) so students have the expected symbol to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks students to implement a function named `print_newline`, but the solution defines a label named `print_nl` instead. The template also does not provide a `print_newline` stub. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual entity (the newline-printing routine) prevents students from clearly mapping the requirement in the problem statement to the implementation in the solution and to any starter code in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent: rename the solution label `print_nl` to `print_newline` (or add an alias label `print_newline` that jumps to/retains the same implementation). Also add a matching `print_newline` stub in the template so students can implement the required function with the exact name used in the problem statement.
